source: Bertolazzi, Tentori, Bernardi (2026) FalsifyBench: Evaluating Inductive Reasoning in LLMs with Rule Discovery Games
finding: Twelve current LLMs play a Wason 2-4-6 style game over WordNet categories: propose test triples, state a hypothesis, guess. Reasoning models beat instruction-tuned ones. Success tracks how often the model tests to falsify its own hypothesis.
numbers: 100 games per model, 12 models (1200 games). Success: GPT-5.2-Chat 75%, GPT-OSS-120B 68%, best instruction-tuned DeepSeek-V3.1 41%, other instruction-tuned 33-35%, GPT-5-Nano 12%, Qwen3.5-9B 21%. Confirmation bias (share of tests that confirm): reasoning models 24-39%, instruction-tuned 66-82%. Conclusive falsification rate GPT-OSS-20B 59.2%, GPT-OSS-120B 53.4%, GPT-5.2-Chat 49.5%, Llama-4-Maverick 18.0%.
quote: models that actively seek to falsify their hypotheses consistently outperform those that primarily seek confirmation
limits: Task is a taxonomy game where the true rule is broader than the first hypothesis (negative testing is optimal by design). Oracle is an LLM (85-95% agreement with humans). Small reasoning models did worse than instruction-tuned ones.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: with 2025-26 models the early failure is in the TEST step, not hypothesis generation: models confirm instead of falsify. The S7 check should force at least one test chosen to break the current rule.

source: Bertolazzi et al. (2026) FalsifyBench, failure analysis section
finding: In failed games the models drift to hypotheses that partly overlap or are disjoint from the true rule, and often switch to surface word features (first letter, vowel count) instead of meaning.
numbers: Failed games had more Partial-Overlap and Disjoint test turns (e.g. GPT-5.2-Chat +27.0 pp, GPT-OSS-120B +22.3 pp, GLM-5 +21.4 pp). Surface-feature hypothesis appeared in 97.6% (GLM-5), 92.0% (GPT-5.2-Chat), 84.4% (GPT-OSS-120B) of failed games; weak models showed no such split (36.4% vs 25.0%, 62.0% vs 47.6%).
limits: Surface-feature detector is a regex heuristic. WordNet stands in for semantic knowledge.
agent_relevance: Second failure mode for S2: hypotheses built on superficial features. A guardrail could ask whether the rule is about meaning or about spelling and format when the task is semantic.

source: Li, Wang, Zheng, Song (2025) Patterns Over Principles: The Fragility of Inductive Reasoning in LLMs under Noisy Observations
finding: Robust Rule Induction task: rules must be induced from examples with some corrupted ones (arithmetic in other bases, ciphers, list functions). Accuracy changes little with noise but which items are solved changes a lot (hypothesis drift).
numbers: List Functions accuracy falls with noise: GPT-4o-mini 31.3 to 19.7 (10 to 30% noise), GPT-4o 39.9 to 26.1, DeepSeek-V3 43.1 to 30.5. Their SRR method: average 64.8 at 10% noise with a 2.8 point drop, versus Hypothesis Refinement 63.6 (6.0 drop) and Self-Consistency 56.0. Table 4 average at 10% noise (GPT-4o / DeepSeek-V3): SC 23.9/63.7, HR initial rule 29.1/63.0, SRR initial rule 36.7/69.5.
limits: Three runs per cell; rules scored by code execution; table text extraction was garbled so per-cell alignment is approximate. Models: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-V3.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: noise handling that works here is (1) induce rules from different SUBSETS of the examples and (2) execute each rule on all examples and feed back the failures. That is close to an exception list: keep a rule that explains most items and list the misfits.

source: Li et al. (2025) Patterns Over Principles: consistency and DeepSeek-R1 results
finding: Even a reasoning model is unstable under noise at instance level: the same task flips between solved and unsolved. Consistency (same instances solved clean vs noisy) is lower than accuracy suggests.
numbers: DeepSeek-R1, Atbash: CoT 65.0 clean, 65.0 noisy (0.0 change) but consistency only 70.0%; SRR 82.0 to 79.0, consistency 93.0%. List Functions: CoT 76.0 to 68.4 (consistency 87.6%); SRR 83.6 to 78.0 (89.6%). Atbash CoT: 15 right-to-wrong and 15 wrong-to-right flips.
limits: One reasoning model, two tasks, 10% noise.
agent_relevance: Accuracy alone hides drift. For S7 (rules still fitting?) track WHICH examples a rule explains, not only the count.

source: Gao et al. (2023) PAL: Program-aided Language Models
finding: Letting the model write code and a Python interpreter run it removes calculation and application errors. The model only decomposes the problem.
numbers: GSM8K: PAL 72.0% greedy and 80.4% with 40 samples and majority vote; abstract: about 15 points absolute over PaLM-540B chain of thought. On Colored Objects, PAL stays near 100% as the object count grows while CoT drops and is unstable.
limits: Codex-era model; arithmetic and symbolic tasks. Needs the rule to be expressible as code.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: cheap reliable rule application means writing the rule as a checkable function and executing it on every example, not re-reading it in prose. Compare the 59.0 to 47.0 ACRE drop when the LM itself applies the rule.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
finding: Sampling several reasoning paths and taking the majority answer beats one greedy path. The paper also discusses ensembling over prompt order as a related approach.
numbers: GSM8K +17.9, SVAMP +11.0, AQuA +12.2, StrategyQA +6.4, ARC-challenge +3.9 points absolute over CoT.
limits: Arithmetic and commonsense QA, not rule induction. Cost scales with samples (40 in the headline numbers).
agent_relevance: Gap 5: voting is a cheap, tested fix for path-to-path variance. Shuffling example order before each vote is the untested rule-induction version.

source: Lu et al. (2022) Fantastically Ordered Prompts and Where to Find Them
finding: Order of the few-shot examples alone moves accuracy from near state of the art to chance. A good order for one model does not carry to another, and no pattern explains good orders. Larger models reduce but do not remove it.
numbers: SST-2: one permutation fell from 88.7% to 51.6% when the model changed (GPT2-XL to another); four-shot spread across permutations from about 50% to about 90%. Entropy-based selection on a model-generated dev set gave 13% relative improvement across 11 text classification tasks.
limits: GPT-2 and GPT-3 era, text classification, not rule induction. Not tested on 2025-26 reasoning models.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: order sensitivity is real in in-context learning, so evaluate rules on held-out examples in several orders and vote. No direct 2025-26 measure for rule induction was found.

source: Chollet, Knoop, Kamradt, Landers (2024) ARC Prize 2024 Technical Report
finding: On ARC-AGI-1 the best systems combine rule induction (program search) and transduction (direct answer); neither alone reaches the top. Plain frontier models without search score low.
numbers: Semi-private / public eval: OpenAI o1-preview 18% / 21%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 14% / 21%, Gemini 1.5 about 5-9%; Greenblatt program sampling 43% / 42%; Berman 53.6% / 58.5%. Kaggle winner the ARChitects 53.5%. Best transduction-only and induction-only single submissions about 40% each.
limits: Written Dec 2024, before later reasoning models. Compute budgets differ across entries (up to $10,000 of API credits).
agent_relevance: Gaps 1-2: large sampling of rule candidates plus execution against the examples (43%) beat a single pass (14-18%). Supports a candidate POOL, but there is no controlled weighting test at equal tokens.

source: Li, Ellis et al. (2024) Combining Induction and Transduction for Abstract Reasoning
finding: Trained induction (write a Python function) and transduction (predict the output) models solve mostly different ARC problems even with the same data, priors and architecture. Ensemble: try induction until a function fits the training pairs, then fall back to transduction.
numbers: ARC validation, GPT-4 descriptions: induction (2048 samples) 18.78%, transduction (beam 20) 15.25%, ensemble 26.50%; GPT-4o-mini descriptions: induction 11.07%, transduction 13.50%, ensemble 19.50%. About 9% of problems fit the training pairs but were wrong on test. Best system on ARC-Potpourri 56.75% vs average human 60.2%.
limits: Trained neural models, not a prompted agent. Synthetic data from GPT-4 and GPT-4o-mini.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: when no rule fits the examples, switch mode instead of keeping a bad rule. About 9% of rules that fit all examples still fail, so a fit check is necessary but not sufficient (S7).

source: Lee, Koh, Lee, Yoon, Kim, Jung (2025) Generating Diverse Hypotheses for Inductive Reasoning (Mixture of Concepts)
finding: Sampling hypotheses independently yields mostly duplicates. A two-step method (list K distinct concepts, then one hypothesis per concept) gets more distinct hypotheses and better accuracy at equal sample count.
numbers: List Functions failed instances, unique programs among K samples: K=2 1.40, 4 1.79, 8 2.92, 16 4.56, 32 7.89. Mixture of Concepts: +4.5 points (GPT-4o-mini) and +5.0 (Llama-3.1-70B) average accuracy over IID sampling with 8 hypotheses. Gains over greedy decoding were small.
limits: Non-reasoning models (GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.1 70B, Qwen2.5 72B). Diversity table alignment is approximate from the text extraction.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: a prompt-level version of opening a new cluster when old ones are covered. Supports keeping several distinct rules at equal sample count; it is not a weighted Dirichlet posterior.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Agents copy the outputs of retrieved past records when the new input is similar (experience-following). Wrong records propagate errors, and even correct but off-distribution records mislead. Deleting records by measured later utility can improve performance and shrink the store.
numbers: Four agents (RegAgent, EHRAgent, AgentDriver, CIC-IoT). With a strict evaluator, history-based deletion improved the real agents; with a coarse or noisy evaluator it could hurt (GPT-4o-mini as evaluator helped EHRAgent, hurt AgentDriver). Combined deletion cut memory roughly 3x with small accuracy change (RegAgent strict: 2938 records vs about 890; 70.95 vs about 66.58 success; table alignment approximate).
limits: Task agents with episodic memory, not rule libraries. Exact table cell alignment uncertain.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: a rule library needs a safe filter: store only validated rules, count later success per rule, delete rules that fail when retrieved. The filter must be strict: a noisy evaluator reverses the benefit.

source: Murphy (2007) Bayesian concept learning (lecture chapter summarising Tenenbaum 1999)
finding: Number game: hypotheses are 40 mathematical rules plus 5050 intervals. Likelihood is (1/size(h))^n (the size principle). Prior weights mathematical concepts 2/3 vs intervals 1/3 (chosen by hand). Predictions average over hypotheses.
numbers: After X={16,8,2,64}: powers of two 1/6^4 = 7.7e-4, even numbers 1/50^4 = 1.6e-7, ratio nearly 5000:1. 'Powers of two except 32' has higher likelihood than 'powers of two' and is excluded only by the prior.
limits: Secondary summary, not the thesis. Human data are shown as figures, not tabulated.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 (partly closed): the arithmetic of the size principle is verified. Among rules that fit all examples, prefer the one allowing the fewest other cases, and keep a prior against odd rules.

source: Tenenbaum (1999) A Bayesian Framework for Concept Learning (MIT PhD thesis), abstract page
finding: Abstract page only (via a fetch summary): prior, likelihood and hypothesis averaging. Under random sampling the likelihood favours smaller consistent hypotheses more with each example, giving similarity-like generalisation after few examples and rule-like after many.
numbers: No numbers. Case studies: continuous feature spaces, word learning, number concepts.
limits: The 2.7 MB PDF download returned HTML, not the PDF; a retry via fetch got HTTP 429. Human-data numbers remain unverified first hand.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: first-hand human numbers are still missing; only the framework is confirmed.

source: Pazzani (1991) Influence of prior knowledge on concept acquisition: experimental and computational results (JEP:LMC 17, 416-432)
finding: Search snippets only: prior causal knowledge changes the rate of concept learning and can dominate the logical form (conjunctive vs disjunctive). The computational side extends explanation-based learning to handle imprecise domain knowledge.
numbers: No numbers obtained. The eScholarship PDF was empty and the scispace copy returned no text.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open: no measured test that explanation-based generalisation beats induction when the theory is partly wrong.

source: Minton (1990) Quantitative results concerning the utility of explanation-based learning (AI 42; AAAI-88)
finding: Search snippets only: PRODIGY/EBL learned control rules can slow the system because matching cost exceeds the savings (the utility problem), so utility must be measured, not assumed. Domains: block stacking, a robot-rooms domain, job-shop scheduling (per a review).
limits: Not opened. A guessed AAAI cdn URL returned an unrelated paper.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: the principle (measure each learned rule's cost and benefit) is supported in outline; use Xiong 2025 (d11) for LLM-agent numbers.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Hypothesis Search: Inductive Reasoning with Language Models (search-result summary)
finding: Search snippets only: the LLM proposes several natural-language rules, filters them, then writes programs. Authors note one try rarely finds a good hypothesis; sampling many works but is costly.
numbers: 40-problem ARC subset: 27.5% vs 12.5% direct (ICLR poster text); v2 reports 30% vs 17%. The versions disagree.
limits: Snippet text only in this pass (the cross-checker opened the paper earlier).
agent_relevance: Gap 1: no equal-token comparison of pool vs single hypothesis was found.

source: Sadeq, Xu, Xie, McAuley et al. (2025) Improving In-Context Learning with Reasoning Distillation (ReDis)
finding: Few-shot prompting of DeepSeek-R1 consistently degraded its performance on inductive tasks. A small model trained to generate rules and follow rules (two separate steps) beats few-shot baselines and in places the teacher GPT-4o.
numbers: LLaMA-3 ReDis relative gains over GPT-4o: 1D-ARC +23.2%, ACRE +2.8%, MiniSCAN +66.6%.
limits: Trained model, so not a scaffold-only result. 7-8B backbones. The R1 degradation claim is in the introduction, with no table opened.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2-3: splitting generate-rule and follow-rule into separate steps with separate checks matches our schema. Rule following was a weak step in Qiu 2024.

source: Bertolazzi et al. (2026) FalsifyBench, related-work pointers
finding: The related-work section cites Jin et al. (2026), saying chain of thought does not reliably help induction and can hurt, and Jhaveri et al. (2026) on confirmation-bias interventions for LLMs. Those two papers were not read.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 follow-up: read Jin 2026 and Jhaveri 2026 before claiming anything about CoT and induction.
